newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes firmer on soybean, corn gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes firmer on soybean, corn gains.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on a strong rally in soybeans and corn, traders said.
"Corn and wheat followed beans, beans were definitely the leader today," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.

The soybean market was boosted to five-month highs on fund buying, concerns about news of a port strike in Brazil and on talk of slow soy harvest in Brazil due to rainy weather. Wheat continued to labor under the weight of large supplies of wheat worldwide and keen competition for wheat export business. Heavy deliveries on the March and scattered stopping of those deliveries trimmed advances in that month.

Commercial selling also was cited with Cargill Inc selling five million bushels of July, traders said. Also, Prudential Securities bought 1.5 million May and E.D. and F. Man bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.

USDA's weekly export inspections data provided little direction. USDA early Monday said 13.459 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended February 27, within the range of expectations from 12.0 million to 15.0 million bushels.
Wheat closed unchanged to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March unchanged at $3.73.

Traders saw no direction from Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report which showed fund longs as of February 25 at 37.22 million bushels and short by roughly 78.86 million bushels.
Nearby March was pressured by the posting early Monday of 2.090 million bushels of wheat for delivery against the March contract and scattered stopping of the deliveries.
Technicians early Monday cited first support in the March at $3.64-1/2 and second support at $3.48-1/2. The session low was $3.70.
First resistance in the March was $3.80-1/2 and second resistance was $3.96-1/2. The session high for March was $3.79.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed at 57-1/2 percent. The trade views a market as overbought with an RSI of 70 or more and oversold at 30 or less.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, above the 17,299 traded Friday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 5,017 traded Friday.
